# KitchenSink4Word

> Everything plus the kitchen sink for Microsoft Word: the most complete Word (.docx) MCP server available. 187 document operations across 108 tools under one grammar, covering live editing of documents open in Word, native citations and bibliography, merge-aware table surgery, footnotes and endnotes, TOC, tracked-changes authoring, Word-native document compare, protection, redaction, mail merge, and accessibility audits. Engineered not to corrupt: atomic validated saves, automatic backups before every mutation, and published adversarial test evidence.

This file describes the shipped release: v2.0.0.
Platform: Windows. File-based tools (the large majority) work without Microsoft Word installed; the com_* and live_* tools use a local Microsoft Word via COM.
MCP transport: stdio.

v2.0.0 is a breaking change from v1.x: every tool name changed as the 189-tool v1.6 surface was consolidated into 108 tools under one verb grammar. The machine-readable rename map is `migration/v1_to_v2.json`; the narrative guide is `docs/MIGRATION_V2.md`; `get_workflows("migrate-from-v1")` returns the map in-session.

## Install

- pip: `pip install kitchensink4word`
- uvx (no install): `uvx kitchensink4word`
- Claude Code: `claude mcp add word -s user -- kitchensink4word`
- Claude Desktop: download `kitchensink4word.mcpb` from the latest GitHub release, then Settings > Extensions > Advanced settings > Install extension (requires uv on PATH)
- Any other MCP client: run the `kitchensink4word` (or `word-mcp`) executable over stdio, e.g. `{"mcpServers": {"word": {"command": "kitchensink4word"}}}`
- MCP registry name: `io.github.nometalalchemist/kitchensink4word`

## Tiered loading (shipped)

A session starts with the 28-tool lite core and enables the rest by pack, on demand:

- `enable_tools(["references"])` turns on a pack; `disable_tools([...])` turns one off.
- Lite-tool refusals for out-of-scope work name the pack and the exact `enable_tools` call to run.
- `get_workflows` recipes name the packs each workflow requires.
- To load everything up front, start the server with `KS4W_MODE=full`.
- Caveat: some MCP clients drop tool schemas on pack disable and do not re-register them on re-enable despite `tools/list_changed`; if a re-enabled tool reports "no such tool", refresh the client's tool list (Claude Code: a ToolSearch call reloads the schema).

## Context cost (measured)

Published because almost no MCP server tells you what it costs to load. Figures come from `scripts/measure_surface.py`:

- Lite core, loaded at session start: 28 tools, about 7,600 tokens.
- Full surface, every pack enabled: 110 tools (108 document tools plus `enable_tools` / `disable_tools`), about 26,600 tokens.
- Versus v1.6 (about 34,400 tokens for the old full surface): roughly 23% less at full load, about 78% less at lite start.
- Clients that defer tool schemas until use (for example Claude Code) pay close to zero until a tool is actually called.

## Capabilities: 108 tools in 8 tiers

### lite core (28 tools, loaded at startup)
Everyday reading and editing: `create_document`, `copy_document`, `get_document_info`, `get_document_view`, `get_outline`, `get_text`, `find_text`, `search_and_replace`, `insert_paragraphs`, `delete_paragraphs`, `set_paragraph_text`, `set_paragraph_format`, `format_text`, `apply_style`, `insert_list`, `insert_break`, `create_table`, `get_table`, `set_cells`, `delete_table`, `delete_element`, `list_elements`, `apply_edits`, `diagnose_document`, `manage_backups`, `get_workflows`, `enable_tools`, `disable_tools`.

### references pack (8 tools)
Citations and bibliography: `insert_citation`, `manage_source`, `set_bibliography_style`, `insert_zotero_citation`, `search_zotero_library`, `convert_citation_style`, `detect_citation_system`, `parse_references`.

### review pack (9 tools)
Tracked changes and comments: `get_tracked_changes`, `resolve_revisions`, `get_revision_report`, `get_comments`, `manage_comment`, `comment_report`, `structured_diff`, `anonymize_for_review`, `deanonymize_document`.

### academic pack (23 tools)
Long-document apparatus: `manage_note`, `convert_notes`, `insert_reference_list`, `insert_caption`, `insert_cross_reference`, `insert_bookmark`, `mark_index_entry`, `assemble_front_matter`, `setup_chapter_headers`, `change_heading_level`, `get_styles`, `define_style`, `get_paragraph_format`, `apply_manuscript_format`, `get_headers_footers`, `set_header_footer`, `set_page_numbers`, `set_section_properties`, `set_document_properties`, `word_count`, `validate`, `prepare_for_submission`, `fix_accessibility`.

### assembly pack (7 tools)
Multi-document work: `insert_document`, `split_document`, `move_section`, `copy_table`, `apply_template`, `fill_template`, `mail_merge`.

### media-forms pack (16 tools)
Images, charts, tables, forms: `insert_image`, `set_image`, `export_images`, `insert_chart`, `set_chart_data`, `insert_equation`, `set_textbox_text`, `insert_hyperlink`, `modify_table_structure`, `set_table_properties`, `format_cells`, `sort_table`, `insert_field`, `insert_content_control`, `set_content_control`, `set_form_fields`.

### com-live pack (13 tools)
Drives a local Microsoft Word: `com_word_status`, `com_refresh_fields`, `com_export_pdf`, `com_import_pdf`, `com_multi_document`, `com_proofing_errors`, `com_readability_statistics`, `com_save_document`, `com_validate_opens_clean`, `live_insert_at_cursor`, `live_scroll_to`, `live_set_track_changes`, `live_repair`.

### protection-io pack (6 tools)
Protection and data I/O: `set_document_protection`, `get_protection`, `set_watermark`, `redact_text`, `import_table`, `export_table`.

## Consolidated multiplexers (how 187 operations fit in 108 tools)

- `list_elements(type=...)`: one tool enumerates every collection (tables, images, charts, footnotes, endnotes, sources, bookmarks, sections, fields, equations, form fields, content controls, lists, TOC, and more) in place of 18 separate v1 listing tools.
- `validate(checks=[...])`: one tool runs any of 14 correctness batteries (core, captions, chapter_headers, cross_references, notes, forms, citation_parity, defined_terms, brand, template, reference_fields, image_resolution, accessibility, redaction).
- `manage_note`, `manage_comment`, `manage_source`, `manage_backups`: lifecycle verbs (insert, edit, delete, and kin) on one object family per tool.
- `modify_table_structure(action=...)`: insert or delete rows and columns, merge, unmerge, split.
- `delete_element(type=...)`: one delete for any addressable element.
- `com_multi_document(action=...)`: compare, combine, or merge documents through Word.

## Recommended workflows

Process reviewer/advisor feedback:
`get_tracked_changes` (see every change with author and text) -> `get_revision_report` (counts by author or type) -> `comment_report` (comments with anchored text and threading) -> `resolve_revisions` (accept or reject, filter by author or type) -> `manage_comment` (resolve threads) -> `validate` (confirm notes and fields survived). Needs the review pack.

Prepare a submission:
`copy_document` (work on a dated copy) -> `validate(checks=["core","citation_parity","reference_fields","cross_references"])` -> `word_count` -> `prepare_for_submission` (accept revisions, strip comments and metadata) -> optionally `anonymize_for_review` for blind review. Re-run the validation after cleanup; the cleanup is itself a mutation. Needs the academic and review packs.

Citation work without breaking the reference manager:
`detect_citation_system` (identify which system owns the citations; mixing them creates a split-brain bibliography) -> `list_elements(type="reference_fields")` -> `validate(checks=["citation_parity"])` -> `convert_citation_style` only when the document is NOT manager-managed -> `validate(checks=["reference_fields"])` afterwards. `insert_citation` and `manage_source` are Word-native; `insert_zotero_citation` is Zotero. Needs the references pack.

Sustained heavy editing:
the user keeps the original open in Word for reading while the agent works on a fresh dated copy at full file-mode speed: `copy_document` -> `get_document_view` (read whole sections cheaply) -> `search_and_replace` -> optionally `apply_edits` (many anchor-addressed edits in one atomic pass) -> `validate` -> `word_count`. No COM round-trips, no lock conflicts. Lite core covers all of it.

## Safety model

- Atomic validated saves; a failed operation leaves the original byte-identical.
- Automatic backup into bounded slots before every file mutation.
- Byte-identical passthrough of anything not being edited (equations, textboxes, content controls).
- Documents open in Word are refused by file-mode tools; the live_*/com_* tools handle that case explicitly.
- Test evidence for v2.0.0: 1,255 tests, adversarial rounds through the raw MCP stdio transport, zero corruptions, verified by opening outputs in invisible Word and failing on any repair prompt.
